verdict.rationale: Warp documents its own pieces for non-interactive automation: a standalone CLI binary installable via Homebrew with no Node.js required [17], a REST API usable from any HTTP client [2], and API-key authentication sent in a header with no interactive login [5]. However, nothing documents running Warp headlessly or in a CI pipeline specifically, and the CLI appears only as a single install line. In-product scheduled jobs [19] are an adjacent feature and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documented CI/headless usage guide, CLI command reference and non-interactive flags, CI examples (e.g. GitHub Actions), and hands-on or independent corroboration.
